passage: Counsellor's note, Monday. Ehsan brought his phone and showed me the weekly report he had found himself: six hours a day, most of it short videos. “I thought it was two,” he said. Then, after a silence, “I'm not going to feel bad about it. I'm going to plan from these numbers.” Together we looked at when the hours happen: on the bus after school and after dinner. He chose to trim only the after-dinner block by an hour for now, and to check the report again on Sunday. His mother, Himani, rang and asked what she could do. I suggested she ask Ehsan about the plan, and not check the phone behind his back. We will look at the numbers again in two weeks. — Nazia

qa.a: Six hours a day, mostly short videos.

qa.a: Shocked, since he had thought it was two hours, but he decided to use the numbers for a plan instead of feeling guilty.

qa.a: Note what he was feeling just before scrolling, since knowing the trigger helps him choose a replacement.

qa.a: Himani is worried and wants to help, so being told to ask about the plan instead of checking the phone gives her a role that keeps trust.

passage:
Tuesday
Aparna Didi dared me to open the screen-time page. I said fine, it'll be about two hours.
Six hours and eleven minutes. Daily average. Four and a half of that on short videos.
I actually felt my face go hot. Six hours is a whole school day. Where did it go? Mostly between 10 pm and 1 am, the report says, and in tiny bits: two minutes, three minutes, forty times.
My usual move would be to feel terrible, delete everything tonight and reinstall on Thursday. Done that twice already. This time I'm going to use the numbers instead. The biggest block is late night, so that's where I start. The short-video app is the main thing, so that gets a limit first, not messages with friends.
Target for this week: under five hours, and nothing after 11.
Checking again Sunday. Numbers, not guilt.
– Nilesh

qa.q: How much of the daily average went on short videos?
qa.a: Four and a half hours of it.

qa.q: How did Nilesh feel on seeing six hours and eleven minutes?
qa.a: Nilesh was shocked and embarrassed, face going hot, realising that was a whole school day.

qa.q: What else could Nilesh look at on Sunday besides the total?
qa.a: When the late-night minutes happened and what came just before, so the next step targets the real trigger.

qa.q: How might Aparna Didi see the result of the dare?
qa.a: Aparna Didi may feel a bit guilty for teasing, but glad the numbers pushed Nilesh toward a real plan.

grounding: Shows a teen shocked by a six-hour daily screen-time report, mostly short videos, deciding to plan from the numbers rather than from guilt.
